items.title: Any worker who can see a shift can download the staff list of that pharmacy, or of its whole organisation, through the shift's member-status page.

items.title: Editing a shift can move it into another owner's pharmacy and overwrite that pharmacy's saved pay rates.
items.test: Tom sends PATCH /api/v1/shifts/<his shift>/ with {"pharmacy": <another org's pharmacy>, "apply_rates_to_pharmacy": true, "role_needed": "PHARMACIST"} and must get 400/403, and the shift's pharmacy and the other pharmacy's rates must be unchanged.

Work notes and calendar events can be moved into, or attached to, a pharmacy or organisation the person has no rights over.
items.test: A staff member PATCHes a work note with another pharmacy's id (expect 403 or no change); an owner POSTs an event with own pharmacy plus a foreign organisation (expect 403)

items.title: Password-reset links are copied into the user's in-app notifications, so anyone holding a signed-in session can take over the account without email access.
items.test: POST password-reset/ for a known user, then assert that no Notification for that user has an action_url (or payload) containing the uid/token reset path.

items.title: Editing chain details removes its pharmacy links
items.test: Create a chain with two pharmacies, submit the web form's multipart PUT changing only its email, and verify both pharmacy links remain.

items.title: Signing out of Expo leaves its push token registered to the prior account, so private alerts can keep arriving on a signed-out device.
items.test: Register an Expo push token while Sara is logged in. Sign out through native app. Trigger a new private message/notification for Sara; assert DeviceToken is inactive or removed and no push sent. Log in as Tom and confirm token belongs only to Tom. Server logout should revoke current device independently of client network reliability.

items.title: Next marketplace and publishing workspaces can display the previous account's private stock, messages or unpublished drafts after cross-tab login.
items.test: Two unrelated owner accounts A/B with separate ethical inventories, goods listings and exchanges. Open A's private pages in tab1, log in as B in tab2 while tab1 remains mounted; simulate slow B getAccess and 403/error, and delay old A promises to finish last. Assert tab1 never renders A names, stock levels or messages once B is authenticated; confirm B sees only permitted data on success and old rows are purged immediately on session change. Repeat with same-tab account switch and logout/reauth. Add publisher A and unrelated user B: open A content workspace and moderation queue in tab1, sign in B in tab2; tab1 must purge all A drafts immediately, while B's server requests are denied. Validate child GoodsExchangeManager rows update when initial data changes instead of using stale initial state.

items.title: Workers browsing shifts can see the names and emails of other workers who are booked on the shift or waiting for payment.
items.test: As Sara (unrelated locum), GET /public-shifts/ and /shifts/{id}/ for a shift where Ben is assigned and Omar is awaiting payment; assert no slot_assignments or payment_options entries and no worker email appear.

items.title: When the owner removes a staff member who is also a pharmacy admin, their admin rights stay on, but when they quit themselves the rights are switched off.
items.test: Owner sends DELETE on an admin's staff membership; afterwards that user must fail the manage-staff and manage-roster checks for the pharmacy and must be missing from the active admin list.

items.title: Re-inviting someone who left as an admin brings back their old admin role the moment they accept a plain staff invitation.
items.test: An admin quits; the owner re-invites them as ASSISTANT; they accept; their old admin record must stay switched off.

items.title: Nothing checks that the person confirming an offer holds the role the shift needs, so a technician or intern can be booked into a pharmacist shift.
items.test: Tom accept_users Ali (OTHER_STAFF, role_type TECHNICIAN, verified, no AHPRA) on a PLATFORM shift with role_needed=PHARMACIST; Ali's offer accept must be refused, and no ShiftSlotAssignment may be created.

items.title: Deleting a restricted Hub group exposes its posts to the whole pharmacy.
items.test: Delete Tom's restricted group containing a post, comment and attachment, then fetch the pharmacy feed as Mia, who was never a group member; verify none of that content becomes accessible.

items.title: Removed Hub group members still receive new private comment text.
items.test: Remove Omar from a restricted group, confirm his post access is denied, then add Mia's comment to his old post and verify no notification or push containing that comment is delivered to Omar.

items.title: Users without pharmacy memberships can overwrite or delete each other's Hub polls.
items.test: Create Sara's public Hub poll with no author membership and existing votes, then PATCH its choices as Zoe without a membership; expect 403 and unchanged choices and votes.

items.title: Revoked invitation sender continues receiving membership response notifications containing staff identities.
items.test: After revoking Lina's organisation/pharmacy authority, make Sara accept/leave. Lina receives no email or in-app notification; valid managers still receive it.

items.title: Authenticated workers can create applications against expired or unauthorised invitation links by calling the generic applications endpoint.
items.test: As unrelated authenticated Sara, POST /api/v1/membership-applications/ with a valid old or disabled invite_link integer, matching her email/DOB/role. Expect refusal and zero application creation; valid UUID magic-link flow must succeed.

items.title: Concurrent mobile logout and in-flight refresh/profile hydration can resurrect old tokens or overwrite the newly signed-in account.
items.test: Defer initial /me success and refresh response; logout or log in as another user before resolving each. Assert no old /me user or refresh token persisted, no old API Authorization and role home remains intended. Repeat native and Expo-web cases, including refresh failures and storage/network exceptions.

items.title: Changing a pending phone number leaves the previous number's verification code usable.
items.test: Issue a phone code for Zoe's number, change her phone through the onboarding update to Tom's number, then submit the original code and assert that Tom's number remains unverified.

items.title: Phone verification replaces a browser-only session with a persistent 90-day session.
items.test: Log Sara in with remember_me=false, complete phone verification, and assert that the replacement auth cookies remain session cookies rather than gaining a persistent expiry.

items.test: Confirm an offer targeting one recurring occurrence and assert no assignments exist for any other occurrence.

items.title: Named public shifts disclose internal pharmacy document links.

items.test: Attempt to replace Omar's payroll assignment with Ben's locum membership; verify approval cannot transfer Omar's employment snapshot to Ben.

items.title: Editing a shift description breaks its pending offers.
items.test: Create a pending offer for Sara with single_user_only=false, submit the description-edit payload, and assert its original slot remains linked and accept succeeds.

items.title: Jobs without dated slots never load internal candidates
items.test: Open a single-worker full-time job with no dated slots and an interested internal member; verify that member appears and can be reviewed.

items.title: A cancelled shift replacement can delete the original shift after an unrelated posting.
items.test: Cancel conversion of Omar's shift, create a separate open shift without leaving the roster page, and assert Omar's original shift and assignment remain.

items.title: Staff on the worker roster can see coworkers' leave type and private leave notes.

items.title: Editing a shift silently replaces custom date rates with calculated rates
items.test: Load a shift with a saved date rate above its guide rate, allow pricing to finish, change only the description, and assert the saved date rate remains unchanged.

items.title: Saving a partially filled shift can delete its confirmed bookings

items.title: Editing a shift replaces its saved per-date rates
items.test: Load an existing shift with an $80 per-date override and a $60 calculated guide; change only its description and assert the submitted rate remains $80.

items.title: Editing a shift after a worker has accepted but before payment either locks the worker into new dates they never agreed to, or takes the payment without booking anyone.
items.test: Create an offer in ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT on a multi-slot shift, PATCH the shift with a new slots payload, then run the fulfilment webhook for that offer id; assert the edit is refused (or the offer is reset for re-confirmation) rather than the webhook failing or the worker being assigned.

items.title: A worker or manager can silently delete a shift offer, including one that is accepted and waiting for payment, so payment can be taken with nobody booked.
items.test: As Sara, DELETE /shift-offers/{id}/ on her ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT offer; assert 405/403 and that the offer still exists.

items.title: Cover requests from the web and mobile worker screens are never linked to the worker's assignment, so approving one never releases the worker.
items.test: Ali has an assignment. POST /worker-shift-requests/ with the exact web payload (no 'shift'), then approve it as Tom. Assert Ali's assignment is released and no second shift is created. Today Ali stays assigned and a new LOCUM_CASUAL shift appears.

items.title: Removing or escalating an assignment from the owner roster page unbooks the worker silently, including paid marketplace bookings, and skips the attendance/leave history check.
items.test: Give Sara an assignment with a linked LeaveRequest or AttendanceSession. Call POST /roster-shifts/<shift>/escalate/ (or DELETE /roster-owner/<assignment>/) as Tom. Assert it is refused, or that Sara is notified and the history is kept. Today the assignment and its leave are deleted silently.

items.title: Accepting a valid counter offer for a vacancy without dated slots crashes

items.title: Marking an invoice paid leaves its balance and cash worksheet unchanged.
items.test: Mark an unpaid $1,100 GST invoice paid through each persona's action and assert that the balance becomes zero and the confirmed receipt appears in the appropriate cash worksheet period.

items.title: Subscriptions remain active after Stripe marks them unpaid.
items.test: After an active subscription's paid period expires, deliver invoice.payment_failed followed by customer.subscription.updated with status unpaid and assert that the subscription response no longer reports active.

items.title: Concurrent claims can award multiple rewards for the same referral.

items.title: Confirmed counteroffers are invoiced using the original shift hours.

items.title: Migration replaces historical invoice billing details with a customer matched only by name.

items.title: Locking a period always produces an empty payroll handoff.

items.title: Both invoice editors block saving an invoice prefilled from an accepted shift.

items.title: Saving an invoice revision removes its recorded receipts from the cash worksheet.

items.title: Legacy Expo invoice generator defaults superannuation to 10% despite Australia's current 12% SG rate.

items.title: Finishing an older invoice email can publish a newer unsent revision.

items.title: Archiving a roster removes its scheduled work and approved leave from timesheets
items.test: Build a timesheet with approved roster-linked annual leave, archive its published roster week, rebuild, and assert rostered and approved-leave minutes remain unchanged.

items.title: Extending an active junior agreement bypasses its birthday rate limit.
items.test: For an active junior agreement ending before the next birthday, PATCH effective_to=null and assert rejection with the original end date preserved.

items.title: Attendance timeline correction modal uses UTC string in local datetime input shifting timestamps
items.test: In a browser running in Australia/Sydney (UTC+10), opening the correction modal for an event at 17:00 local time and submitting should send an effective timestamp of 17:00 AEST (07:00Z) rather than shifting 10 hours to 07:00 AEST (21:00Z previous day).

items.title: Rejecting provisional attendance permanently blocks the whole timesheet period.
items.test: Reject Omar's closed provisional attendance, rebuild his timesheet and attempt period locking after all payable hours are approved; assert that the rejected evidence does not leave an unresolvable approval blocker.

items.title: Saving employment terms leaves existing timesheets using stale pay agreements.
items.test: After approving Omar's timesheet containing today's work, create successor terms effective today and assert locking fails until recalculation and renewed approval.
